10.1002_adfm.78195: Nickel‐cobalt‐based hydroxides have established their niche in stationary storage applications where high theoretical capacitance, affordability, and carbon footprint matter most. Nonetheless, realizing their high rate capability and enduring cycling stability are challenged, originating from sluggish electron transfer and inadequate mechanical strength. Here, we pioneered to leverage on atomically uniform Cu‐incorporation via light illumination to optimize the electronic and atomic structure of amorphous CoNi hydroxide. Remarkably, the as‐fabricated amorphous CuCoNi hydroxide electrode embraces an ultra‐high rate capacity of 74.1% following a 50‐fold increase of current density and an unprecedented cycling life (∼ 92.6% of the initial capacitance retention after 100 000 cycles at 10 mA cm −2 ), far exceeding performances reported in the literature. The exceptional electrochemical performance could be attributed to Cu introduction, which leads to the transfer of more electrons from Ni to Co during the energy storage process, facilitating Ni in achieving the tetravalent state and obtaining additional pseudocapacitance. Additionally, the Cu‐incorporation could effectively induce the appearance of defect states and lower the adsorption energy of OH − , thus expediting surface redox reactions. This atomic structure tuning strategy may shed light on the electrode material design for high‐performance energy storage devices.
10.1002_aenm.202504330: All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) are gaining attention due to their high safety and energy density compared to those of conventional lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, insufficient contact between the cathode active material (CAM) and solid electrolyte (SE), or using a high proportion of SE in the cathode, hinders energy density improvements. Maintaining a low electrolyte proportion while ensuring sufficient Li‐ion pathways is challenging. This study elucidates the correlation between SE particle size distribution and electrode microstructure, as well as Li‐ion and charge transfer kinetics. A spray‐recrystallization method is introduced to control the size of SEs. Exquisite SE size control allows the intimate interface between CAM and SE as well as homogeneous SE distribution, enhancing Li‐ion transport kinetics and corresponding to reducing charge transfer resistance (R ct ) and Li‐ion migration resistance (R ion ). A full cell with an NCM/SR‐LPSCl cathode shows a reversible capacity of 171.6 mAh g −1 , 74.1% cycle retention after 100 cycles, and 113.7 mAh g −1 at room temperature. It is confirmed that the cathode containing 90 wt.% NCM and a high areal capacity of 15 mAh cm −2 is maintained stably, and the impact of the particle distribution of sulfide‐based SEs on R ion and R ct .
10.1002_smll.74502: The selective generation of the electrophilic oxidant singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) in the photo‐Fenton process is crucial for achieving precise control over organic pollutants in environmental applications. Herein, we rationally designed a CuS/MoO 3 (CM‐1.0) heterojunction featuring a coherent heterojunction interface characterized by Mo‐O‐Cu covalent bridging bonds and a low lattice mismatch of 1.04%. This design significantly enhances the intrinsic electric field strength of CM‐1.0 (54 times that of MoO 3 and 195 times that of CuS) and the separation efficiency of photogenerated charge carriers. Simultaneously, benefiting from rapid electron transfer between Cu sites (O‐Cu) and H 2 O 2 under alkaline conditions, the in‐situ formation of transition metal complexes (O‐Cu‐OOH) is facilitated. This composite achieves nearly 100% selective production of 1 O 2 while scavenging electrons from ·O 2 − (electron donor), thereby enabling a rapid tandem reaction of H 2 O 2 ‐ 1 O 2 . Experimental results have shown that CM‐1.0 achieves a 99.2% removal rate of tetracycline (TC) within 10 min, with a first‐order kinetic constant ( k obs ) of 0.3814 min −1 . Furthermore, through experiments with different water quality conditions, under actual sunlight exposure, and in flow systems demonstrate that the system exhibits excellent interference resistance, excellent stability, and potential for practical remediation applications.
10.1002_smll.76401: Germanium (Ge) is a promising anode material for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) owing to its high theoretical capacity and superior electronic conductivity, yet its practical application is severely hindered by drastic volume expansion during cycling. To address this issue, a Ge thin‐film anode is deposited onto a pre‐synthesized hollow carbon nanobox@Cu (CB@Cu) current collector, which enables synergistic interface‐mass transfer‐mechanical modulation. The introduced CB interlayer favorably reduces the electron tunneling barrier and optimizes current distribution, enhancing electrode conductivity. The hollow porous carbon architecture ensures sufficient electrolyte penetration and intimate electrode/electrolyte contact, accelerating Li + diffusion kinetics. Meanwhile, the internal void space effectively accommodates volume expansion of Ge, maintaining solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer integrity over prolonged cycling. Consequently, the Ge@CB electrode delivers a reversible capacity exceeding 1000 mAh g −1 and exhibits superior rate capability up to 10 A g −1 , significantly outperforming the Ge electrode without CB modification. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations elucidate the synergistic mechanism, demonstrating an effective strategy for high‐performance thin‐film anodes.
10.1016_j.coelec.2026.101875: Electrochemical layer-by-layer characterisation (LbL-EC) is emerging as a transformative strategy for designing robust, high-performance electrochemical (Bio)sensors. By enabling in-operando real-time control of multilayer assembly, LbL-EC permits precise tuning of film thickness, composition, and bioreceptor orientation, thereby enhancing sensitivity, stability, and durability. Techniques such as cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, applied individually or synergistically, provide dynamic insights into deposition processes, interfacial charge transport, and surface loading density while minimising nonspecific interactions. This review examines the mechanisms governing mass and charge transport within polyelectrolyte multilayers and critically explicates the strengths and limitations of LbL-EC in building supramolecular architectures for advanced biosensing. Comparative discussion with conventional imaging methods, including transmission electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and scanning tunnelling microscopy, highlights the unique ability of LbL-EC to couple structural precision with functional optimisation. Collectively, LbL-EC is positioned as a pivotal enabler of next-generation (Bio)sensors with unprecedented reliability and performance.
10.1016_j.est.2026.122541: Lithium-ion capacitors combine the characteristics of lithium-ion batteries and supercapacitors to achieve high energy and power densities. We analyze the effects of slow charging and electrode mass balancing on the power, energy, and cyclability of lithium-ion capacitors. Results show that graphite-activated carbon lithium-ion capacitors can simultaneously achieve high energy and power densities under optimized slow-charging protocols. Specifically, energy densities ranging from 60 to 104 Wh kg −1 and power densities of 20–113 kW kg −1 (maximum measured) or 1.7–14.5 kW kg −1 (practical) can be achieved depending on electrode mass ratio and operating protocol. Energy density can be increased through basic cell engineering without compromising power density. However, adjusting garphite-activated carbon electrode ratio to 1:3 reduces cell power and is not beneficial. Cyclability under slow charge conditions depends on the discharge current. If the discharge current is insufficiently elevated, lithium depletion in the negative electrode occurs, leading to poor cyclability. The combination of slow charging and fast discharging extends cyclability to 150,000 cycles for a 1:1 electrode ratio. The study reveals distinct performance regimes in lithium-ion capacitors under slow charge conditions: an ultra-high-power regime achieved by limiting charging current, and a high-energy and ultra-high-power regime achieved by increasing the positive electrode content and limiting charging current. Cyclability improves by fine-tuning lithium intercalation and deintercalation through appropriate balancing of charge and discharge currents. This study bridges a significant research gap and improves understanding of lithium-ion capacitors. The findings offer actionable strategies for customizing electrode ratios and charge-discharge cycles to achieve targeted application goals. • Operation of lithium-ion capacitors under slow charge conditions is investigated • Exceptionally high practical power densities are measured (14.5 kW kg −1 ) • Simultaneously enhanced energy and power densities are possible • Two performance regimes for ultra-high power are identified • Good cyclability requires avoiding lithium depletion in the graphite electrode
10.1038_s41467-026-69391-3: Overcoming the inherent limitations of perovskite-perovskite heterojunctions in simultaneously boosting built-in potential and suppressing non-radiative recombination remains a critical challenge in perovskite solar cells. Here, we introduce a ferroelectric-based heterojunction architecture that addresses this dual challenge through synergistic mechanisms. Firstly, the spontaneous polarization inherent to the ferroelectric-based heterojunction significantly amplifies the built-in electric field, enhancing charge separation and transport, thereby increasing open-circuit voltage from 1.16 to 1.21 V. Secondly, ferroelectric nuclei effectively regulate perovskite crystallization kinetics via dissolution-recrystallization modulation, effectively suppressing trap states and elevating fill factor from 83.6% to 86.8%. The champion devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.62% (certified 26.07%) with an open-circuit voltage-fill factor product of 1.05 V, reaching 90.3% of the Shockley-Queisser limit. Furthermore, the modified devices demonstrate enhanced operational stability with over 85% efficiency reservation after 500 h of maximum power point tracking, charting clear pathways towards high-performance photovoltaic cells. Wu et al. report a strategy of incorporating either Dion-Jacobson phase or Ruddlesden-Popper phase ferroelectric perovskite with FAPbI3 to form bulk heterojunctions, increasing the open-circuit voltage-fill factor product and enabling single junction solar cells with an efficiency of 26.62%.
